meta.purpose: Disjoint-rebuild floor for LanceDB: floor = tear(genR2, genR3) which shares NO build with the recall-matched pair (genA, genB). Also reproduces the shared-genB floor (genB, genR2) and MEASURES whether optimize()/rebuilds perturb the row order.

constructions.matched: (genA, genB): genA=fresh create_index, genB=post-optimize rebuild. Shares genB with shared_floor.
constructions.disjoint_floor: (genR2, genR3): two further create_index(replace=True) rebuilds. Shares NO build with matched.
constructions.shared_floor: (genB, genR2): reproduces the matched2 floor. Shares genB with matched.

order_preservation.method: Read the physical id sequence from the underlying lance dataset (table.to_lance().to_table(['id'])) at four points: after create_index (genA), after optimize() (genB), after rebuild#2 (genR2), after rebuild#3 (genR3). Compare each later sequence to the genA sequence by exact equality, longest common prefix and sha256.

caveats.isolated_floor_construction: disjoint_floor = tear(genR2, genR3) shares NO build with matched (genA, genB); this is the estimate isomorphic to pgvector's independent-rebuild floor. shared_floor = tear(genB, genR2) is the matched2 floor and shares genB with matched (correlated); it is reported only as a control.
caveats.recall_level_dependence: tear_eq depends strongly on the operating recall level; compare only at matching targets. The matched row and the two floor rows are all aligned by pick_pair to the same target R over each side's grid.
caveats.gap_can_miss: the 3-seed worst case can miss |gap|<=0.004; per-seed reached flags and gap ranges are reported.
caveats.row_order_measured: order_preservation is MEASURED by comparing the physical id sequence (table.to_lance().to_table(['id'])) before/after optimize() and after each rebuild; see order_preservation.all_preserved.
caveats.grids_used: HnswFlat used the dense grids (gridA=168, gridB=141). IvfPq used a trimmed grid (gridA=80, gridB=12) because the dense ivfpq grid (~120-224 settings) pushed one seed past the single-command budget; the two families therefore differ in grid density, which only affects how close each target is bracketed (report the per-row gap). Note the matched2 data itself was produced with grids that differ from the current script file (matched cells: hnsw gridA=216/gridB=101, ivfpq gridA=120/gridB=70), so the matched rows here are internally consistent with THIS run's disjoint floor rather than byte-identical to the earlier matched rows.
